newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said two news conferences scheduled in Rome on Tuesday would be retransmitted to the Breydel press room. One will be on the inter-governmental conference with Commission President Jacques Santer, Dutch Prime Minister Hans van Mierlo, Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and European Parliament President Jose-Maria Gil-Robles at 1300/1200 GMT. The other will be on the 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome with Santer and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi at 1700/1600 GMT. Vale de Almeida noted that the Commission would hold its weekly meeting in Rome at 1730/1630 GMT.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said the Commission wanted Japan to open specific markets as part of its final round of deregulation measures. Noting that the EU had submitted a list of 200 requests in November, he said some progress had been made in areas including insurance, electrical equipment and air transport. But more progress was needed, for example on restrictions against foreign horses participating in horse races.

Vale de Almeida said there was hope at the General Affairs Council for an accord allowing South Africa to join the Lome Convention since Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes had made some positive statements. He said the ministers were finalising conclusions on the issue. (see BC-TRADE-SAFRICA)

Guilford said the ministers had approved the global Information Technology Agreement, which would be discussed at a World Trade Organisation meeting in Geneva on Wednesday. He said the first tariff cuts would take place next July.

He said the ministers urged the Commission to submit concrete proposals for helping the least developed countries have greater access to the world trading system and briefly discussed OECD talks on a multilateral accord on investment. He said one of the EU's negotiating objectives would be to make sure the agremeent did not enable the extraterritorial application of national laws.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/247: EU calls for final push on deregulation in Japan
- Speech/97/72: "The European Social Fund: Starting a New Millenium" by Commissioner Padraig Flynn.
- Speech/97/73: "The future of European agricultural policy and rural development" by Commissioner Franz Fischler.
